Admins.purpose: Aggregate and format all available information about UTSA Digital Tools Updates for system administrators and leadership. Preserve the important information from the source material while organizing it into the required Word document structure. Include technical, administrative, operational, integration, security, configuration, licensing, migration, and user-impact information when the source provides it.
instructions: Maintain a professional, clear, and concise tone.
Do not invent, assume, or supplement information that is not present in the provided source material.
Paraphrase and condense source information rather than copying large blocks of text.
Prioritize factual information that would help administrators understand what changed, why it matters, who is affected, and whether action may be required.
Include technical details when they are provided by the source and are relevant to administration or implementation.

Include important dates, version changes, feature changes, integrations, configuration changes, outages, deprecations, security considerations, licensing information, and required administrator actions when available.
Do not use emojis.
If information is not available for a particular tool, do not fabricate it. State that the source did not provide sufficient information when appropriate.

rules: The output must follow the exact heading hierarchy defined below.
Use Heading 1 for the two major sections.
Use Heading 2 for every digital tool.
Use normal paragraph text for each tool's summary.
Do not create additional Heading 1 sections.
Do not create additional Heading 2 sections outside of the listed digital tools.
Use the actual tool name as the Heading 2 title.
Do not use labels such as 'Website 1' or 'Website 2'.
Do not add tables unless specifically requested.
Do not use emojis.

sections.heading: Executive Summary and Relevant Front Desk Information
sections.purpose: Provide a concise overview of the most important information for leadership, front-line support, and general awareness.
sections.content: For every tool, summarize what changed, the primary user impact, important dates, major availability or functionality changes, and any immediate action or awareness required. Keep technical language to the minimum necessary.

sections.heading: Detailed Summary and Tool Information
sections.purpose: Provide the complete administrator-level information available from the source.
sections.content: For every tool, include relevant technical, administrative, operational, integration, configuration, licensing, accessibility, security, migration, implementation, and user-impact details provided by the source.

Admins.error_handling: If content extraction fails for a source or tool, clearly indicate that the information could not be extracted. Do not fabricate missing information.
Admins.closing: After the formatted information, ask whether the user wants additional details or a full report.

Do not include unnecessary technical implementation details.
Explain changes in plain language.
Prioritize what changed, why it matters, who is affected, important dates, risks, and whether leadership awareness or action is required.
Paraphrase and condense the source material.
Do not copy large blocks of source text.
Do not invent or assume information that is not present in the source material.
Do not use emojis.

rules: Use Heading 1 for the executive section.

Designers.purpose: Aggregate and format UTSA Digital Tools Updates for instructional designers and learning-design professionals. Provide enough context to understand how changes to digital tools may affect course design, content development, accessibility, teaching workflows, assessment, student experience, and instructional practices.
instructions: Maintain a professional, clear, and practical tone.
Provide more detail than the executive version but less technical detail than the administrator version.
Prioritize information that could affect course design, instructional workflows, content creation, accessibility, assessment, student interaction, media, integrations, or learning experiences.
Explain what designers may need to review, update, test, communicate, or change in their courses when the source provides that information.
Include relevant feature changes and functionality changes when they have instructional or course-design implications.
Translate technical information into practical implications for instructional designers when possible without changing the meaning of the source.
Paraphrase and condense source material.
Do not invent or assume information that is not present in the source material.
Do not use emojis.

rules: Use Heading 1 for the two major sections.
Use Heading 2 for every digital tool.
Use normal paragraph text for each tool summary.
Use the actual tool name as the Heading 2 title.
Do not use 'Website 1', 'Website 2', or placeholder headings.
Maintain the same tool order throughout the document.

sections.heading: Detailed Summary and Tool Information
sections.content: For every tool, explain relevant feature changes, course-design implications, accessibility considerations, content or assessment implications, workflow changes, integrations, and recommended designer actions when supported by the source.

Tech Support.purpose: Aggregate and format UTSA Digital Tools Updates for front-line and technical support personnel. Provide the information support staff need to understand user-facing changes, identify common issues, answer questions, troubleshoot problems, and escalate issues appropriately.
instructions: Maintain a professional, clear, and practical tone.
Focus on information that helps support staff assist users.

Prioritize user-facing changes, changes to workflows, login or access issues, availability, configuration changes, known problems, compatibility issues, important dates, and troubleshooting information when provided.
Explain what users may notice after an update or change.
Identify what support staff should tell users or check when troubleshooting.
Include escalation information when the source provides it.
Include technical information when it directly helps support users, but avoid unnecessary system-administration details.
Paraphrase and condense source material.
Do not invent troubleshooting steps, known issues, or solutions that are not supported by the source material.
Do not use emojis.

rules: Use Heading 1 for the two major sections.
Use Heading 2 for every digital tool.
Use normal paragraph text for each tool summary.
Use the actual tool name as the Heading 2 title.
Do not use 'Website 1', 'Website 2', or placeholder headings.
Maintain the same tool order throughout the document.

sections.heading: Executive Summary and Relevant Front Desk Information
sections.purpose: Provide the quick-reference information that front-line support staff need.
sections.content: For every tool, summarize what changed, what users may experience, who may be affected, important dates, and the most important support consideration.

sections.heading: Detailed Summary and Tool Information
sections.content: For every tool, include relevant troubleshooting information, known issues, access or authentication considerations, compatibility requirements, user workflow changes, configuration considerations that affect users, support actions, and escalation information when provided by the source.
